question: In OneStream security, which term describes an object that users are assigned to, which then allows those users to access other objects?
explanation: B is correct: a Group is the object that users are assigned to in OneStream, and through that Group assignment, users gain access to other objects. A is incorrect — a User is a person who has access to OneStream; users are assigned to Groups. C is incorrect — a Role is a predefined set of permissions for specific actions or pages. D is incorrect — an Object is an item in OneStream that security is applied to.

question: In OneStream, which security term describes a predefined set of permissions used to assign access to specific actions or pages?
explanation: C is correct: a Role is a predefined set of permissions used to assign access to specific actions or pages in OneStream. A is incorrect — a User is a person with access to OneStream. B is incorrect — a Group is what users are assigned to in order to access other objects. D is incorrect — an Object is an item in OneStream that security is applied to.

question: What are users assigned to in the OneStream application to receive access to objects?

options.B: System and Application roles in OneStream.

explanation: C is correct: in OneStream, users are assigned to Groups to receive access to objects. The Group is the intermediary between users and the objects they can access. A is incorrect — users are not directly assigned to objects; Group membership grants that access. B is incorrect — users are assigned to Groups, not Roles, to access application objects. D is incorrect — Cube View Profiles control access to Cube View Groups, not the primary user access mechanism.

question: How is dimension security different from security on other objects in OneStream?

options.A: Dimension security does not use Access Groups and Maintenance Groups.
options.B: Additional security options are available on dimension members to limit access to data.
options.C: All dimension members include the Display Member Group security property.
options.D: Dimension security is applied at the cube level rather than the member level.

explanation: B is correct: dimension security is unique because additional security options are available on dimension members to limit access to data — options not available on other object types. A is incorrect — dimension security does use Access Groups and Maintenance Groups. C is incorrect — the Display Member Group property is not present on all dimension members. D is incorrect — dimension security operates at the individual member level.

question: A consultant is copying a user account to test a user's security. Which property category should be modified to configure the new account as a native (non-SSO) user?
explanation: C is correct: the Authentication property category is where the External Authentication Provider must be set to (Not Used) and the Internal Provider Password must be entered to configure the account as a native user. A is incorrect — General contains basic user information, not authentication settings. B is incorrect — Status controls whether the account is active or inactive. D is incorrect — Preferences controls UI preferences, not authentication type.

question: Which group naming convention structure makes it easy to see all security groups created for an Entity member listed together under Administration | Security | Groups?
explanation: C is correct: E_Europe_View and E_Europe_Write places the entity name (Europe) immediately after the E_ prefix, so groups sort alphabetically together. A is incorrect — placing the access type first (E_View_, E_Write_) separates groups for the same entity. B is incorrect — inconsistent naming would not keep all entity groups together. D is incorrect — omitting the E_ prefix removes the standardized entity identifier.

question: Which two properties on an Import workflow profile must be updated to prevent users from importing data while still allowing them to see the Import workflow profile? (Select 2.)
explanation: A and C are correct: the Access Group controls who can see the workflow profile, and the Workflow Execution Group controls who can execute it. Updating both prevents execution while permitting visibility. B is incorrect — Certification SignOff Group controls workflow certification, not import execution. D is incorrect — Workflow Name is an identifier, not a security property.

question: Which tabs in the Security Builder Template workbook are used to create an XML file that can be loaded into OneStream?

options.A: User Security Design, WF Load-Certify Security, and WF Profile Security Design.
options.B: Instructions, WF Load-Certify Security, and Entity Security Design All.
options.C: Instructions, User Security Design, and WF Load-Certify Security.
options.D: User Security Design, WF Profile Security Design, and Entity Security Design All.

explanation: D is correct: the User Security Design, WF Profile Security Design, and Entity Security Design All tabs generate the XML file loaded into OneStream. A is incorrect — WF Load-Certify Security is not an XML-generating tab. B is incorrect — the Instructions tab is a reference guide, not an XML generator. C is incorrect — the Instructions tab does not generate XML.

question: Which entity property must be set to True for slice security to be active in OneStream?
explanation: C is correct: Use Data Cell Access Security must be set to True on the entity to activate slice security, which restricts which specific data cells a user can see or edit based on group membership. A is incorrect — Is Consolidated controls consolidation participation. B is incorrect — Is IC Entity marks an entity as intercompany. D is incorrect — Allow Adjustments controls journal adjustment permissions.

question: A consultant's application has four cubes. One cube contains sensitive HR data that should only be visible to a special group of users. What should the consultant do?

options.A: Secure the HR cube using the Cube Properties.
options.B: Secure the Entity dimension to restrict access.
options.C: Secure the Account dimension to restrict access.
options.D: Create a separate application for the HR cube.

explanation: A is correct: cube-level security is configured through the Cube Properties, where Access Groups and Maintenance Groups restrict which users can see or interact with the specific cube. B is incorrect — Entity dimension security restricts access to specific entities across cubes, not to a whole cube. C is incorrect — Account dimension security restricts account access, not cube-level access. D is incorrect — creating a separate application is unnecessary overhead when cube-level security handles this within a single application.

question: A consultant needs one group to see and edit Actual data, and another group to see and edit Budget data. No read-only access is required. There is one Actual member and one Budget member. How many security groups should be created?
explanation: B is correct: one group with full see-and-edit access for Actual, and one group with full see-and-edit access for Budget = 2 groups total. A is incorrect — four groups would be needed if read-only access was also required (View and Write groups for each of two scenarios). C is incorrect — one group cannot separately control access for two different sets of users on two different scenarios. D is incorrect — three is not a logical number given two scenarios and no read-only requirement.
